title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of Beacon Minerals Limited. Subject to the Non Trading Period ban, the active/speculative dealing ban and the third-party financial products ban; may seek exceptional-circumstances approval or a waiver from the Managing Director (or, if absent, the Company Secretary).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of BCN. Same substantive restrictions as employees; distinguished for exceptional-circumstances approval and policy waivers (Chairman) and for the Listing Rule 3.19A duty to report changes in their interest in BCN securities.

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: The Managing Director; distinguished only in that exceptional-circumstances approval to deal during a Non Trading Period is given by the Chairman.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board; distinguished only in that exceptional-circumstances approval to deal during a Non Trading Period is given by the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouses or de facto spouses, dependants under 18, and any other person or arrangement (e.g. a trust) in which the employee or director is or is to be treated as interested for Corporations Act purposes.

windows.start_anchor: commencement of the 2 week period preceding the announcement of the annual results, half yearly results, or the quarterly cash flow statement (Appendix 5B)
windows.end_anchor: the statement has been lodged on the ASX announcements platform

windows.start_anchor: prior to the making of any JORC Resource and/or Reserve Statement
windows.end_anchor: the statement has been lodged on the ASX announcements platform

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Managing Director or the Chairman may extend or shorten a Non Trading Period, or introduce another Non Trading Period, at any time, notified to employees by email and to directors by email and/or facsimile, effective immediately on notice; confidentiality of the notice is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified ban on dealing at any time in financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks (warrants, futures or other financial products), whether traded on ASX or any other market. No clearance or waiver mechanism is cross-referenced in this section; the only carve-out is for a listed portfolio or index product containing BCN securities.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as warrants, futures or other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions traded on either ASX markets or any other market.

rules.detail: Hedging is never named as such, but a hedging instrument written by a bank over BCN securities would be a 'financial product ... issued over BCN securities by third parties' and so is caught by the absolute ban in section 4.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as warrants, futures or other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions traded on either ASX markets or any other market.

rules.detail: A monetisation structured as a bank-issued instrument over BCN securities (e.g. a prepaid forward) is a 'financial product ... issued over BCN securities by third parties' and banned under section 4. A plain agreement to sell the underlying shares themselves (no third-party product) would instead just be an ordinary Dealing under section 2/3, restricted only by the Non Trading Period and active-dealing rules.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as warrants, futures or other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions traded on either ASX markets or any other market.

rules.detail: Short selling of BCN shares themselves is not named; it is not clearly caught by the third-party financial products ban (which targets instruments issued by banks/institutions, not the employee's own short sale) and would only be restricted if it amounted to frequent, regular 'active dealing'.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
A CFD referencing BCN shares, written by a bank or broker, falls within the catch-all 'other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties' and is banned.
rules.evidence: Employees and directors are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as warrants, futures or other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions traded on either ASX markets or any other market.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over BCN securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Secured financing arrangements in respect of BCN securities are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

Ban on 'actively' dealing in BCN securities with a view to deriving profit-related income during a Trading Period, defined as dealing in a manner involving frequent and regular trading activity; no fixed holding period is prescribed.
rules.evidence: Dealing during a Trading Period is subject to the prohibition that an employee and director must not actively deal in BCN securities with a view to deriving profit related income from that activity. "Actively Deal" for this purpose means to deal in BCN securities in a manner which involves frequent and regular trading activity.

clearance.evidence: the Managing Director, in his discretion to the Chairman to deal during the Non Trading Period.

short_term.evidence: "Actively Deal" for this purpose means to deal in BCN securities in a manner which involves frequent and regular trading activity.

exceptions.evidence: An exception may apply where BCN securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director or Company Secretary (employees); Chairman (directors and Managing Director); Managing Director (Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: If there are exceptional circumstances, for example a pressing financial commitment, then approval may be given by: the Managing Director or if absent, the Company Secretary, in their discretion to an employee to deal during the Non Trading Period

exceptions.approver: Managing Director or Company Secretary (employees); Chairman in consultation with Managing Director (directors)
exceptions.evidence: If there are exceptional circumstances, the Managing Director or if absent, the Company Secretary, in their discretion may waive parts of this policy to allow for employees to deal. If there are exceptional circumstances, the Chairman in consultation with the Managing Director, in his discretion may waive parts of this policy to allow directors to deal.

exemption_authority: The Managing Director (or, if absent, the Company Secretary) may in their discretion approve an employee's dealing during a Non Trading Period, or waive parts of the policy for an employee, in exceptional circumstances such as a pressing financial commitment; the Chairman has the equivalent discretion for directors (in consultation with the Managing Director for a section 5 waiver), the Chairman approves the Managing Director's dealing, and the Managing Director approves the Chairman's. Approval must be obtained in advance and cannot be given retrospectively, and a section 5 waiver must be recorded and reported to the Board at its next meeting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and directors are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as warrants, futures or other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions traded on either ASX markets or any other market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This absolute ban, with no waiver mechanism referenced, squarely covers a bank-structured OTC put and call over BCN shares, meaning the derivative legs of a funded collar cannot be entered into under the policy as drafted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An exception may apply where BCN securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bespoke bilateral bank collar is not a listed portfolio or index product, so this narrow carve-out cannot be used to structure around the section 4 ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any such approval must be obtained in advance. It cannot be given after the event.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for ordinary share dealing during a Non Trading Period, collar entry or unwind approval must be secured before execution; retrospective ratification is unavailable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: BCN may require an employee to provide confirmation of dealing in BCN securities by an employee or his/her associate(s).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: BCN can demand after-the-fact confirmation of any collar transaction entered into by the executive or an associate, including one routed through a spouse or trust.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a waiver has been granted the details of the same must be recorded and reported to Directors at the next Board meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any section 5 waiver permitting collar-related dealing becomes visible to the full Board, so confidentiality of the arrangement cannot be assured.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy as drafted: section 4 imposes an absolute, unqualified ban on employees and directors dealing 'at any time' in financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks - precisely the OTC put and call a bank would write - with no clearance, waiver or hardship mechanism referenced in that section. The only stated carve-out is where BCN securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product, which would not cover a bespoke bilateral collar. The policy is also silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance, so there is no established approval route for a loan secured on the collared shares either. Ordinary dealing in the underlying shares themselves (without a third-party derivative) is otherwise permitted outside the two-week pre-results/Appendix 5B and JORC Non Trading Periods, subject to advance, non-retrospective exceptional-circumstances approval (Managing Director for employees, Chairman for directors) to deal within those windows and a ban on frequent, profit-driven active dealing. The bank should not proceed with a funded OTC collar unless BCN's Board first amends section 4 or grants (and reports to the Board) an express waiver of it.
